text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Macedonian government is expected to issue soon an international tender for offers from consulting firms interested in the privatisation of Macedonian Telecommunications. The consulting companies should be included in the legal and financial aspect of the venture. A decision is expected by end September.

- By the end of March 1998, Macedonia is expected to withdraw or use the second instalment of the credit for structural reforms approved by the World Bank valued at $60 million. One of the terms for the approval of the credit is adoption of a law on denationalisation estimated at $1.5 billion.

- The U.N. Special human rights rapporteur, Elisabeth Rehn, will sumbit a report to the Human Rights Committee no later than September 30 which will include Gostivar events. In April, Macedonian foreing ministry asked that Macedonia be excluded from Rehn's mandate.

- Sofia submitted a new proposal for resolving the language dispute with Macedonia, proposing that agreements between Macedonia and Bulgaria be signed in the "Bulgarian language" and in the "official language of the Republic of Macedonia, which, by its constitution, is defined as Macedonian."

- The number of enrolled university students of nationalities other than Macedonian has risen significantly. Of the total 4,110 enrolled in the first round at the Cyril and Methodius University, 283 are Albanians, 52 Turks, 109 Serbs and 80 Vlachs.

- Senior Macedonian government official said if the U.N. Security Council proposed that Macedonia be registered under the name "Republic of New Macedonia" in the world organisation, the Macedonian government will withdraw from U.N. membership.

- As of today, the central warehouse will start with the delivery of a new shipment of medicines intended for state hospitals and public pharmacies in Macedonia. Apart from the clinical hospital, priority will also be given to the delivery of medicines to tourist centres in Macedonia.
